invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Search boxes with the joined blue icon button on the party pickers and transporter list, the transporter list filtering as you type, and 'Add a transporter' beside the search, in both frontends
increments.detail: The designers found the address picker and transporter search boxes look different (S26, S33). The prototype draws one search control everywhere: a box with a square blue search icon button joined to it, under a medium 'Search' label. Main has a smaller box with a separate grey 'Search' text button under it. A real icon submit button works without JavaScript and is allowed by the 9 October afternoon ruling (claims 24-25). This row gives every server search in both frontends that look: the five animals party pickers, the plants consignor, place of destination and consignment contact pickers, and the animals transporter list. Search still runs on the server when the button or Enter is pressed. Filtering or listing as you type stays out for the party pickers (waiting-on-design inc-193). The transporter list now filters as you type (Sam, 20 Oct: "another one for the blue icon and same behaviour as the rest"): with JavaScript its rows narrow as the trader types, with matching letters in bold, and without JavaScript today's box you submit stays, its blue icon button submitting the search. This carves req-389 and criterion 3 out of blocked transporters inc-037. The commodity search is not in this row: Sam blocked it on 20 October until the MDM commodity API and the commodity type-ahead component land, and its look moved to inc-014. This row carries inc-086's search criteria (criteria 3 and 4). openspec: live-animals/addresses, plants/addresses, plants/journey-pages consignor-select, place-of-destination and consignment-contact-select, and live-animals/journey-pages/transporter: the search runs from a 'Search' icon button. Consolidated 20 October 2026: this row also places 'Add a transporter' on the transporter list's search row, above the table, which was inc-211 (S27). It is the same search row on the same page, so it is built, tested and reviewed once here.
acceptanceCriteria: On the five animals party pickers and the plants consignor, place of destination and consignment contact pickers, the search label 'Search' is medium, and the hint 'Name, address or country' stays. On those pickers and the animals transporter list, the search runs from a square icon button joined to the right of the box, whose accessible name is 'Search' (Welsh as today); there is no separate 'Search' text button. With JavaScript off, pressing the icon button or Enter in the box narrows the list on the server, as today, on every one of those pages. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-035; screens/prototype/S26--default--nojs.png shows the prototype does not)

Given the transporter list with JavaScript on, when the trader types in its search box, then the table shows only the rows that match as they type, by name, address, approval number, type or status, with no page reload and no Search press, and focus stays in the box. (Sam, 20 Oct; req-389, req-390 as today's server filter matches; theme:transporters inc-037 criterion 3)

Given a filtered transporter list, when rows match, then the letters that match in each shown cell are in bold, drawn by the same escape-then-bold helper as the type-ahead suggestions (inc-202), so a name with '&' shows as written. (Sam, 20 Oct: same behaviour as the rest)

Given the trader is filtering the transporter list, when the shown rows change, then a polite live region says how many are shown, such as '3 transporters shown', or 'No transporters match', with Welsh machine drafts. A transporter already chosen stays chosen when it is filtered out of view, as the hidden selected field keeps it today. (WCAG 4.1.3; transporters.njk selected field)

Every changed page has no serious or critical accessibility violations, empty, searched and with no matches. (repo:frontend; repo:plantsfrontend)

On the transporter list the secondary 'Add a transporter' button sits on the search row, aligned to the right, above the transporter table, and no longer below it; on a phone it sits below the search. The transporter list has no serious or critical accessibility violations. (repo:frontend)

Each page is one POST form and the mojSearch macro emits its own form, so put MoJ's input-wrapper and icon-button classes on govukInput and govukButton (the button as the input's after-input slot, MoJ's aria-hidden, unfocusable svg plus visually hidden 'Search' text), and import MoJ's search stylesheet in each frontend's application stylesheet. Data source, 20 Oct: the transporter list is not from the address book or a backend. The frontend ships its transporters in services/transporters/records.js and keeps the ones an organisation adds in an in-memory map (register.js), and partiesFor(orgId) joins them: a handful of rows. The server already renders the whole list into the page when nothing is searched. So the filter narrows the rows rendered in the page; it needs no endpoint and no new API. If transporter management (inc-037) later moves the list to the address book or a backend and it grows large, revisit this there.

Control call: the transporter list is a table of radios with address, approval number, type and status columns, not a single pick list, so the accessible-autocomplete library does not fit it: wrapping it would drop the columns traders compare. "Same behaviour as the rest" is built as the same look (the joined blue icon), the same as-you-type narrowing and the same bold matches, with the bold helper shared with inc-202's wrapper. The filter is a small progressive-enhancement module in the existing client bundle.

Saved animals appear above the fields rather than below (S17). A 'You have entered details for all …' message appears that the prototype does not have (S18). identification-and-permanent-address inc-046, inc-047 and inc-050 already plan the grouping, the panel's save and layout, and the identifier labels and hints, and move in here. What no row planned is the look: each species in a bordered box with a grey header bar holding its name and 'Change number of animals', the page at full width, and regular-weight identifier labels. increments.title: CPH number: three labelled boxes as drawn, no cursor jump, and the whole number kept when typed or pasted in one go, in animals
increments.detail: The designers asked for the cursor to jump to the next CPH box when one is full (S37). Sam ruled on 20 October: no cursor jump. Moving focus while someone types fails WCAG 3.2.2 unless users are told first, and GOV.UK forms do not do it. The real problem the designers saw is that typing the 9 digits straight through keeps only '12': each box has a maxlength of 2, 3 or 4, so the browser drops every keystroke after County is full. This row keeps the prototype's three boxes, each with a visible label and styled as drawn, and drops the maxlength cut-off so nothing typed or pasted is lost. When County holds the whole number and Parish and Holding are empty, the server splits it into the three parts on save. That works without JavaScript and needs no new client script. The prototype's own digit filter and paste spreading stay in waiting-on-design inc-093. openspec: live-animals/journey-pages cph-number: no automatic focus moves; the whole number typed into County is kept and split on save.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the CPH number page on a live-animals notification, when it shows, then the 'CPH number' question has three boxes in one row, each with a visible label ('County', 'Parish', 'Holding number', Welsh as today), 2, 3 and 4 characters wide, laid out and styled as the prototype draws them. (review:designers-2026-10-19 S37; prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/cph-number.html p9-011; screens/prototype/S37--all-typed-continuously.png)

Given the CPH number page, with JavaScript on or off, when the trader fills a box, then focus stays in that box: nothing moves focus to the next box, and Backspace in an empty box does not move focus back. (Sam, 20 Oct: no cursor jump; c-006; req-713 out of scope)

Given the CPH number page with JavaScript off, when the trader types '123456789' straight through into County, then County shows all nine digits; no box cuts typing short. (review:designers-2026-10-19 S37; screens/main/S37--whole-number-typed.png shows only '12' kept today)

Given County holds '123456789', '12/345/6789' or '12 345 6789' and Parish and Holding are empty, when the trader presses Save and continue, then the number is saved as 123456789 and the consignment addresses page shows it as 12/345/6789. (review:designers-2026-10-19 S37; req-2122)

Given the trader pastes '12/345/6789' into County, with JavaScript on or off, when they press Save and continue, then it is saved as 123456789, the same as typing it, and focus never moved while pasting. (review:designers-2026-10-19 S37; req-2122)

Given County holds something that is not 9 digits once spaces and slashes are removed, such as '1234', and Parish and Holding are empty, when the trader saves, then today's per-part error messages show and the boxes keep what was typed. (req-715; c-114)

notes: Approach chosen: drop the maxlength attributes and let the server split a whole number typed or pasted into County, rather than a script that spreads a paste across the boxes. It is the only one of the two that works without JavaScript, it adds no client script to the page, and it covers typing straight through as well as pasting. The 2, 3 and 4 widths still show the number's shape.

Server: when Parish and Holding are empty and County, with spaces and slashes removed, is exactly 9 digits, split it into 2, 3 and 4 before the existing per-part checks. Anything else goes through today's checks unchanged.

Tests: the fit spec asserts maxlength 2, 3 and 4 today (cph-number.fit.spec.js:99-106). Change those asserts to the widths and add the typed-in-one-go and pasted cases, with JavaScript on and off. Add the same in trade-imports-ins-tests tests/animals/e2e for the CPH page, and the validate unit tests for the split.

Not in this row: the hint wording ('For example 12/345/6789'), the autocomplete and pattern attributes and the blank save are consignment-parties inc-091. This row changes the same template, so whichever lands second rebases.
